advances: A finite compactly supported measure identity, including atoms. The density ratio is restricted to positive-density intervals.

proof:
The prescribed vector divergences sum to zero. Deleting an edge, set its flow to the negative sum of the divergences on the tail component. For any vertex the components on the other side of its incident edges partition the remaining vertices. Summing the signed flows there therefore gives its prescribed divergence. The directed path formula follows by this construction. For any scalar vertex function $h_z$, expansion by the edges gives $\sum_e F_e(h_{\rm head}-h_{\rm tail})=\sum_z w_z(m_z-m)h_z$. This proves the tree-independent formula for $J$. Separating $L-m$ as $(L-m_z)+(m_z-m)$ in each closed tail gives the first identity. For $t\ge m_z$, the fiber centered integrand is nonnegative on the tail. For $t<m_z$ the integral is the negative of the nonpositive integral over the strict lower tail, since the full centered integral is zero. Thus the positivity and identity include closed-cap atoms.

Choose a scalar $A$ strictly below the supports. Use $\phi(x)=\phi(A)+\int_A^x\phi'(t)\,dt$ (or choose $A$ in the neighborhood immediately below the support interval). In each fiber the centered constant vanishes. Fubini on a bounded interval gives its $\kappa_z$ term. The difference between two normalized expectations kills the same constant, so applying the same argument to each edge gives the $J$ integral. The edge coupling expression is the fundamental theorem of calculus applied between its two scalar values and integrated. Distributionally the derivative of $t\mapsto\int_{[t,\infty)} h(x)\,d\nu_z(x)$ is $-h(t)d\nu_z(t)$, by testing with smooth compactly supported derivatives and Fubini. Apply this to the fiber centered term and the tree-independent expression for $J$. In the volume case, coarea of the affine scalar map gives the stated $f_z$. The derivative formulas follow immediately from the distributional identities with their absolutely continuous measures. The local product derivative is exactly that of $\sum_z\kappa_z+J$ on intervals where the ratio is defined.

For the finite cap menu project the vector divergence to each $a_j$. Apply the scalar closed-tail identity at threshold $b_j$ and sum with weights $\lambda_j$. This yields the displayed joint flux and keeps all individual tail fractions in the coefficients.

statement:
Let $\mu=\sum_z\mu_z$ be a finite positive measure supported on finitely many compact fibers, with $\mu_z$ lifted to its labeled base and of positive mass $w_z$. Write $g_z$ for its normalized fiber barycenter and $g$ for the global barycenter. On any oriented spanning tree of the labels let $G_e$ have incoming-minus-outgoing divergence $w_z(g_z-g)$. For $L(w)=a\cdot w$, write $\nu_z=L_\#\mu_z$, $m_z=a\cdot g_z$, $m=a\cdot g$, $F_e=a\cdot G_e$, and
$$
P_z(t)=\nu_z([t,\infty))/w_z,\qquad
\kappa_z(t)=\int_{[t,\infty)}(x-m_z)\,d\nu_z(x),\qquad
J(t)=\sum_e F_e(P_{\rm head}(t)-P_{\rm tail}(t)).
$$
Then $\kappa_z\ge0$ and $J(t)=\sum_z w_z(m_z-m)P_z(t)$ is independent of the tree. On a consecutive directed path through $z_1,\ldots,z_N$, $F_j=\sum_{i\le j}w_{z_i}(m-m_{z_i})$. For every real $t$, with the threshold atom included,
$$
\int_{L\ge t}(L-m)\,d\mu=\sum_z\kappa_z(t)+J(t).
$$
For every $C^1$ function $\phi$ on a neighborhood of the compact scalar support interval,
$$
\int(L-m)\phi(L)\,d\mu
=\int\sum_z\kappa_z(t)\phi'(t)\,dt+\sum_e F_e(\mathbb E_{\rm head}\phi(L)-\mathbb E_{\rm tail}\phi(L))
=\int[\sum_z\kappa_z(t)+J(t)]\phi'(t)\,dt.
$$
For any coupling $\pi_e$ of the normalized tail and head scalar laws, the edge expectation difference equals
$$
\int\int_0^1(x'-x)\phi'((1-r)x+rx')\,dr\,d\pi_e(x,x').
$$
In the distributional sense, $d\kappa_z=(m_z-t)d\nu_z$, $dJ=-\sum_z(m_z-m)d\nu_z$, and $d(\sum_z\kappa_z+J)=(m-t)d\sum_z\nu_z$.

For ordinary $d$-volume on full-dimensional convex fibers and continuous normal $u\ne0$ in $L(z,x)=v\cdot z+u\cdot x$, write $f_z(t)=\mathcal H_{d-1}(K_z\cap\{L(z,x)=t\})/|u|$, $f=\sum_z f_z$, and $R=\sum_z(m_z-m)f_z$. Almost everywhere, $P_z'=-f_z/w_z$, $(\sum_z\kappa_z)'=(m-t)f+R$, and $J'=-R$. On any open positive-density interval away from scalar fiber endpoints, $\tau=(\sum_z\kappa_z+J)/f$ obeys $(\tau f)'=(m-t)f$ almost everywhere.

For a finite menu of closed caps $H_j=\{a_j\cdot w\ge b_j\}$ and weights $\lambda_j\ge0$, use the same $G_e$ throughout. Let $P_{zj}=\mu_z(H_j)/w_z$ and $\kappa_{zj}=\int_{H_j}a_j\cdot(w-g_z)\,d\mu_z$. Then
$$
\sum_j\lambda_j\int_{H_j}a_j\cdot(w-g)\,d\mu
=\sum_{z,j}\lambda_j\kappa_{zj}
+\sum_eG_e\cdot\sum_j\lambda_j a_j(P_{{\rm head},j}-P_{{\rm tail},j}).
$$
title: Closed-tail Stein decomposition and common vector tree flux for finite fibers
